conclusions: The uniform sample does not support a global claim that publisher boxes are too loose. Their median area is slightly smaller than both visible-all-parts reviewer sets. Some crowded outliers are larger, some smaller.

Foot/head inclusion and ambiguous occluded-body ownership create real extent disagreements; masks also exhibit actual merges, fragments and detector duplicates. Neither phenomenon excuses every strict failure.

These labels remain useful for the unchanged conservative joint naming-plus-localization benchmark. Its score is not a separately measured biological-name accuracy. Do not change failed metrics, thresholds or denominators.
Both AI reviews themselves contain errors/uncertainty. The error-selected earlier35-case review and this uniform diagnostic answer different questions; neither certifies99% biological identity.

Next independent validation needs pre-prediction visible-instance masks or clearly defined visible boxes, verified animal identities and temporal entry/exit/reconnect coverage in a new recording, with true human/domain review. Preserve this exposed dataset as regression only.
